title: SHE FORGOT HER WATER JAR.
paragraphs:
The one thing she came for.
The reason she walked to the well under the burning noon sun—
when no other women would be there.

Pause there.
Because that jar wasn’t just pottery.

Five husbands behind her.
A man in her house who wasn’t her husband.
A reputation that whispered through the streets of Samaria like smoke.

So she came at noon.
Alone.
A Jewish rabbi… speaking to her—a Samaritan woman with a scandal attached to her name.
And He didn’t start with condemnation.

From water…
to worship…
to truth.
And then Jesus touched the wound she tried to bury.
Because the One speaking to her already knew everything…
Then came the moment that changed her life:
“I who speak to you am He.” — John 4:26
Standing in front of the most unlikely witness in Samaria.
And suddenly the jar didn’t matter anymore.
“Then the woman left her water jar, went back to the town and said to the people…” — John 4:28
“Come see a man who told me everything I ever did!”
That jar stayed by the well.
Because when you meet the Living Water…
you stop carrying the things you once needed to survive.
Some of us are still gripping our jars.

Shame.
Secrets.
Old identities.
The labels people gave us.
But Jesus is still sitting at wells today.
Still offering living water that satisfies the deepest thirst of the human soul.

We all have a past.
We all carry jars.
But Jesus Christ came to seek sinners, reveal truth, and give new life through His cross and resurrection.
Grace does what shame never could.
So maybe today is the day you drop the jar.
Because the Savior who knew everything about her…
is the same Savior who died and rose again for you.
“Whoever drinks the water I give will never thirst.” — John 4:14

—
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
